podcast.title: Devotional Tour Breakdown and Replacement (1993)
podcast.body: During the recording of "Songs of Faith and Devotion," Andy Fletcher exhibited signs of severe depression and was sent home from sessions. On the Devotional Tour, he was depressed, homesick, and hypochondriac, suffering a nervous breakdown that led to a month-long hospitalization, causing him to miss the entire second leg of the tour. He was replaced by keyboardist Darryl Bata Montey for 39 shows. "He suffered a nervous breakdown and had to be checked into the hospital for a month, missing the entire second leg of the tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Breakdown on Exotic Tour (1994)
podcast.body: During Depeche Mode's 1994 Exotic Tour, which became known for its debauchery, Andy Fletcher experienced a breakdown two months into the tour and was forced to return home. His role was then taken over by Daryl Bamonte, who had been part of Depeche Mode's road crew since their early days. "Depeche survived two months before he had a breakdown and needed to go home."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

podcast.title: Post-Tour Financial Issues and Death (1994-2022)
podcast.body: After the tumultuous 90s, Andy Fletcher managed to regain stability and continue as a functioning member of Depeche Mode, despite facing financial issues from bad investments, which he also survived. Sadly, he died at his home on May 26, 2022, at the age of 60, from an aortic dissection, a sudden and massive internal bleeding event. "But then Fletcher died of an aortic dissection in his home on May 26, 2022."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Anxiety, Depression, and OCD Diagnosis
podcast.body: In 1989, Andy Fletcher of Depeche Mode began suffering from significant anxiety, leading to diagnoses of depression and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD). He sought treatments and generally managed his conditions effectively. "In 1989 he started suffering from a lot of anxiety and he was diagnosed with depression and OCD."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

podcast.title: Coping Mechanisms and Personal Life (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: Andy Fletcher attempted to decompress from band stress by playing chess, becoming quite skilled. He also ventured into entrepreneurship by opening a restaurant named Guesconi near Abbey Road Studios in London, which ultimately failed. He became a father for the first time in August 1991, adding more pressure to his life. "He also opened a restaurant in London called Guesconi near Abbey Road Studios, but that failed to arrest some mental health challenges he was having."

podcast.title: Mental Health Struggles (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: Andy Fletcher was diagnosed with OCD, which he believed was inherited from his father, and also struggled with anxiety and depression, requiring professional treatment. He found Dave Gahan's ego trip particularly difficult to manage, contributing to a "three against Dave" dynamic within the band. "He was diagnosed with OCD, something he believed he inherited from his father."

xref.title: Long-Term Recovery and Current Status (1997-Present)
xref.body: Depeche Mode eventually overcame the tumultuous period between 1991 and 1997. Dave Gahan and Martin Gore are now sober, and Alan Wilder is living a quiet life. While Andy Fletcher died in 2022, Martin Gore and Dave Gahan continue to record and tour together, showing intent to move forward almost 50 years after the band's formation. "The good news is that the Pesh mode eventually came out on the other side of all things that happened between 1991 and 1997."

xref.body: Andy Fletcher of Depeche Mode died in 2022 from an aortic dissection, the same undiagnosed condition that caused the death of Lux Interior of The Cramps. "This is the same thing that killed Andy Fletcher of Depeche Mode in 2022."

xref.title: Andy Fletcher's Mental Health Struggles
xref.body: Like many other rock stars, Andy Fletcher experienced problems with anxiety and depression, developing a severe case of OCD in his early 20s which worsened after his sister's death. His mental health was particularly poor in 1993 and 1994. "Like so many other rock stars, Andy had problems with anxiety and depression."

xref.title: Andy Fletcher's Sudden Death and Cause
xref.body: Andy Fletcher died suddenly at his home on May 26, 2022, from an aortic dissection, a condition where the inner layer of the largest artery in the body tears, allowing blood to leak out and potentially rupture completely, leading to immediate death. "Andy died suddenly at his home on May 26, 2022, of something called an aortic dissection."

xref.title: Aortic Dissection Shared by Other Artists
xref.body: Andy Fletcher's cause of death, an aortic dissection, is the same condition that also claimed the lives of actors John Ritter and Alan Thicke, as well as musicians Lux Interior of The Cramps and Peter Steele of Type O Negative. "This is the same thing that killed actors John Ritter and Alan Thick. And it also killed Lux interior singer for the cramps and Peter Steele of the bad typo negative."

xref.title: Cause of Death: Aortic Dissection
xref.body: Andy Fletcher's cause of death was an aortic dissection, a rare condition that is seldom diagnosed in advance due to few warning signs and can result from factors like high blood pressure or congenital conditions, leading to rapid internal bleeding. "Cause of death was an aortic dissection, a rare condition that's almost never diagnosed in advance because there's no real reason to look for it because there are a few, if any, warning signs."

xref.title: Crucial for Tour Completion
xref.body: Daryl Bamonte's intervention was critical for Depeche Mode, as his willingness to fill in for Andy Fletcher enabled the band to complete one of the biggest tours of their career, which would otherwise have been cut short. "Without him, Depeche mode would not have been able to finish one of the biggest tours of their career."

xref.title: Early 90s Struggles
xref.body: In the early 1990s, Depeche Mode was in a "very bad place" largely due to extensive drug and alcohol use. Martin Gore suffered severe seizures, leading doctors to suspect a brain tumor. Andy Fletcher (Fletch) experienced debilitating panic attacks, and keyboardist Alan Wilder quit the band due to the stress. Singer Dave Gahan was heavily addicted to heroin and cocaine. "In the early 90s, Depeche Mode was in a very bad place. Thanks to lots and lots and lots of drugs and alcohol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Gasconi – Andy Fletcher's London Italian Restaurant
xref.body: Andy Fletcher of Depeche Mode, along with his wife Grania, opened an Italian restaurant called Gasconi in the mid-1990s in the St. John's Wood area of London, near Abbey Road recording studios and Violet Hill. The restaurant, located at one Blenheim Terrace, was intended as a distraction for Andy due to the adverse effects of Depeche Mode's extensive touring, which had caused him to miss part of a tour previously. It became a pilgrimage site for Depeche Mode fans, and Martin Gore, the band's songwriter, was a frequent visitor. Andy eventually sold his stake in Gasconi to focus on his record label, Toast Hawaii, and occasional DJ gigs. "Gasconi was supposed to be something that could distract him between Depeche Mode projects."

xref.title: Official Statement on Passing
xref.body: Depeche Mode released an official statement indicating that Andy Fletcher died at home, naturally and without suffering. "The official statement from Depeche Mode is that Fletcher died at home, naturally and without suffering."

xref.title: Rarity of Aortic Dissection
xref.body: Aortic dissection is a rare condition, affecting approximately three out of every 100,000 people annually, with men being more susceptible than women, and the average age for such an event being 63. Andy Fletcher was 60 when he died. "Only about three and a hundred thousand people are hit with such a thing every year."
